data.name: Dolph
data.gender_notes: Dolph is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Greek word ‘δολφις’ (dolphis), meaning ‘swimmer’. In Greek mythology, the dolphin was a symbol of the god Apollo and his son Asclepius, and was believed to have the power to heal. The name Dolph carries the meaning “Swimmer” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Dolph usually hope their child will grow to embody swimmer and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength, courage, and the power of healing.
data.etymology: Dolph belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Swimmer.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Dolph total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: The name Dolph may have originated from the ancient Greeks, and its original meaning, ‘swimmer’, beautifully illustrates the connection between this name and the sea. In contemporary culture, Dolph may be seen as a strong and powerful name, evoking images of the graceful and intelligent creatures that share his name.

The dolphin was believed to have the power to heal, making it a powerful and auspicious symbol for those named Dolph. The name may evoke an innate sense of peace, intelligence, and wisdom, inspiring those who bear it to pursue a deeper connection to the natural world and to use their gifts to heal and inspire others. Also, in Christian perspective, Dolph reminder us of the miraculous powers of Jesus which heals the sick, raises the dead and does other miracles as shown time and time again in the bible.
